item.title: Herdr on Windows: the Differences ConPTY Brings, Six Explicitly Unsupported Capabilities, and the Cursor versus IME Dilemma
item.description: Go item by item through Herdr 0.9.2's Windows support boundary against the documentation: the install path and the stable/preview channel rules (an existing preview install stays on preview, and migrating takes two steps), the two paste methods in Windows Terminal, the cursor dilemma under ConPTY where host_cursor auto actually means drawn cells and switching to native trades flicker for an IME anchor, live cwd being unreliable under PowerShell while OSC7 works, Kitty graphics being unavailable in Windows Terminal, agent process-tree detection following Git Bash exec boundaries, the 12 supported Windows integrations, plugins being preview only on Windows, and the six explicitly unsupported capabilities — direct attach, live handoff, Unix fd handoff, foreground process groups, the clipboard image bridge, and signed binary/SmartScreen avoidance — with what each one means for your actual workflow. Baseline herdr 0.9.2.

item.title: Herdr Troubleshooting Checklist: 11 Real Failure Modes, and Why the "Just Restart" Remedy Kills Your Processes in Four of Them
item.description: Rewrite the 11 documented troubleshooting entries as symptom, root cause, remedy, and cost: the misplaced CJK IME window and the host_cursor trade-off, Enter/Tab/Backspace firing twice plus the minimum fixed version of each terminal, Option+arrow printing ;3D and the zsh bindkey fix, an updated binary with an old running session, macOS Keychain failures and why launchctl managername must be checked first, SSH or DNS failing after a macOS logout, and why herdr server stop exits every pane process, plus where the logs actually are. Verified locally: log paths, HERDR_LOG, config check, and launchctl output. Baseline herdr 0.9.2.

item.title: Module 5: Troubleshooting and Tuning (diagnosis order, 208 configuration keys, Windows boundaries)
item.description: The full Herdr troubleshooting and tuning guide: the 11 documented failure modes reorganised by who owns the problem, and why herdr server stop ends every pane process; 208 configuration keys across 14 sections, the division between client-owned and server-owned settings, three tiers of when a change takes effect, the real rules of headless sizing, the trade-offs in the three terminal keys, the decoupling of update.manifest_check from detection rules, and a risk ranking of the 7 experimental keys; the differences ConPTY brings on Windows, the 20 explicitly supported capabilities and the 6 explicitly unsupported ones, the two dilemmas of live cwd and cursor versus IME, the 12 Windows integrations, and plugins being preview only on Windows. Baseline herdr 0.9.2 stable.

item.title: Zorin OS 18 Review: I Switched, and I Never Missed Windows
item.description: After ten years on Windows, what scares you most about switching? It's not learning something new—it's that feeling of total disorientation. Zorin OS 18 tackles exactly that.

item.title: Running Rust Async on Windows? Meet the Little Devil in the Closet: Device Afd
item.description: Why does Rust async work on Windows? Unveiling Microsoft's undocumented AFD driver with real-world analogies to understand Windows async programming under the hood
